sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When Warren Furatani was growing up in Los Angeles in the 1950s,
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代，当沃伦·富谷在洛杉矶长大时，

sentences.en: he sometimes heard his parents refer to a place they once spent time.
sentences.zh: 他有时会听到父母提到一个他们曾经待过的地方。

sentences.en: A place they called camp.
sentences.zh: 一个他们称之为“集中营”的地方。

sentences.en: You know, camp reference for me was summer camp or the Y camp.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我对“集中营”的认知就是夏令营或者基督教青年会夏令营。

sentences.en: So what is this camp thing they keep talking about?
sentences.zh: 所以他们老挂在嘴边的这个“营”到底是什么东西？

sentences.en: The fact that it's brought up here and there, but not elaborated on.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这个词总会被偶尔提及，却没有详细的解释，

sentences.en: You can't help but wonder, there must be much more to the story.
sentences.zh: 你禁不住会想，这个故事背后一定还有更多内容。

sentences.en: Warren was right.
sentences.zh: 沃伦猜得没错。

sentences.en: There was a lot more to the story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事背后的内容多得多。

sentences.en: Producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: During World War II, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 二战期间，美国

sentences.en: government incarcerated Warren Furatani's parents,
sentences.zh: 政府将沃伦·富谷的父母，

sentences.en: along with over 110,000 other Japanese Americans in remote detention centers.
sentences.zh: 以及其他11万多名日裔美国人关押在偏远的拘留中心。

sentences.en: When they talked about camp, that's what they meant.
sentences.zh: 当他们谈起“集中营”时，指的就是这个。

sentences.en: In college in the 1960s, Warren got involved in the civil rights movement
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代上大学时，沃伦投身于民权运动

sentences.en: and the Asian American movement.
sentences.zh: 和亚裔美国人运动。

sentences.en: And as he got more politically active, he started to research his people's history.
sentences.zh: 随着他政治参与度越来越高，他开始研究自己族群的历史。

sentences.en: He wanted to find out what had happened to his parents
sentences.zh: 他想弄清楚他的父母

sentences.en: and other Japanese Americans during the war.
sentences.zh: 以及其他日裔美国人在战争期间遭遇了什么。

sentences.en: One day, he was at a Vietnam War protest with his friend Victor Shibata.
sentences.zh: 一天，他和朋友维克托·柴田一起参加一场反越战抗议活动。

sentences.en: And they started talking about how they wanted to organize a march
sentences.zh: 他们开始讨论如何为

sentences.en: for the Asian American community.
sentences.zh: 亚裔美国人社区组织一场游行。

sentences.en: But they didn't know where to go.
sentences.zh: 但他们不知道该去哪里。

sentences.en: And Victor and I said, well, there's these camps that our parents were in.
sentences.zh: 维克托和我当时说，嗯，我们父母当年被关在那些集中营里。

sentences.en: What are these camps?
sentences.zh: 这些集中营到底是什么？

sentences.en: We started talking to some people about this place called Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 我们开始跟一些人聊起一个叫曼扎纳的地方。

sentences.en: It was the closest camp to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 那是离洛杉矶最近的集中营。

sentences.en: And we said, damn it, we better just go up there and just find it.
sentences.zh: 我们当时说，该死，我们最好直接去那儿找找看。

sentences.en: It wasn't going to be easy to find.
sentences.zh: 要找到它可不容易。

sentences.en: After World War II, Manzanar had been completely dismantled.
sentences.zh: 二战结束后，曼扎纳已经被完全拆毁。

sentences.en: By 1969, there were hardly any signs of it left.
sentences.zh: 到1969年，那里几乎找不到任何痕迹了。

sentences.en: But Warren and Victor spoke with some people from their parents' generation
sentences.zh: 但沃伦和维克托与他们父母那辈的一些人交谈过后，

sentences.en: and learned that the camp had been located a few miles past the town of Lone Pine
sentences.zh: 得知集中营位于隆派恩镇外几英里处、

sentences.en: off Route 395, and that a big green auditorium building was still standing,
sentences.zh: 395号公路旁，而且那里还矗立着一栋绿色的大礼堂建筑，

sentences.en: being used by the highway department to store machinery.
sentences.zh: 正被公路部门用来存放机械。

sentences.en: And so, on a clear fall day,
sentences.zh: 于是，在一个晴朗的秋日，

sentences.en: the two men hopped in Victor Shibata's old Triumph convertible
sentences.zh: 这两个年轻人跳进维克托·柴田的老旧凯旋敞篷车里，

sentences.en: and went looking for this place called Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 出发寻找这个名为曼扎纳的地方。

sentences.en: They drove north out of LA about four hours
sentences.zh: 他们从洛杉矶向北开了大约四小时车，

sentences.en: toward the Sierra Nevada Mountains and ended up in a high desert valley.
sentences.zh: 朝着内华达山脉开去，最终来到一个高地沙漠山谷。

sentences.en: It was totally desolate.
sentences.zh: 这里彻底是一片荒凉。

sentences.en: But a few miles outside of Lone Pine, they found the green building
sentences.zh: 但在隆派恩外几英里处，他们找到了那栋绿色建筑，

sentences.en: and they turned off the highway onto a small dirt road.
sentences.zh: 于是他们从公路拐进了一条狭窄的土路。

sentences.en: Tumbleweeds, no trees, a lot of underbrush.
sentences.zh: 滚球草，没有树木，到处都是灌木丛。

sentences.en: And in the background was the Sierra Nevada Mountains covered in snow.
sentences.zh: 背景则是积雪覆盖的内华达山脉。

sentences.en: It was as dramatic a landscape as you could imagine.
sentences.zh: 这是你能想象到的最具戏剧性的风景。

sentences.en: The two men continued driving through the desert,
sentences.zh: 两个年轻人继续开车穿过沙漠，

sentences.en: and then suddenly they came across an old white pillar with Japanese lettering on it.
sentences.zh: 然后突然撞见了一根上面写着日语字样的古老白色石柱。

sentences.en: It just was stunning, just like it was waiting there to be discovered.
sentences.zh: 简直令人惊叹，就像它一直在那里等待被人发现一样。

sentences.en: It was the original pillar marking the Manzanar Cemetery,
sentences.zh: 这是标记曼扎纳墓地的原始石柱，

sentences.en: and it was surrounded by faded gravestones of people who had died while in the camp.
sentences.zh: 周围环绕着在集中营关押期间去世的人们那褪色的墓碑。

sentences.en: As they explored the area further, Warren and Victor eventually came across a big pile of debris.
sentences.zh: 随着对该地区的进一步探索，沃伦和维克托最终发现了一大堆废墟。

sentences.en: And we found all of these broken dishes, and on the back of the dish said Army dinnerware with dates on it.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了所有这些碎盘子，盘子背面写着带有日期的军队餐具。

sentences.en: And different things we found.
sentences.zh: 以及我们发现的各种其他东西。

sentences.en: It was like an archaeological day.
sentences.zh: 就像进行了一次考古探索的日子。

sentences.en: It revealed this historical reality called camp.
sentences.zh: 它揭示了被称为“集中营”的这段历史现实。

sentences.en: The two young men had found the remains of a camp that only a few decades earlier
sentences.zh: 这两个年轻人找到了一个集中营的遗迹，仅仅几十年前，

sentences.en: had imprisoned over 10,000 Japanese Americans.
sentences.zh: 这里曾关押过一万多名日裔美国人。

sentences.en: And in the process, they were helping uncover a dark chapter in U.S.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，他们正在帮助揭开美国历史上黑暗的一页，

sentences.en: history
sentences.zh: 一段历史

sentences.en: that a lot of people at the time would have rather forgotten.
sentences.zh: 当时许多人宁愿将其遗忘。

sentences.en: The incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II
sentences.zh: 二战期间对日裔美国人的关押，

sentences.en: wasn't even mentioned in most high school history textbooks in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 在60年代的大多数高中历史教科书里甚至都没有提及。

sentences.en: There was no books, no stories, no information, couldn't find it in the card catalog in the library.
sentences.zh: 没有书，没有故事，没有信息，在图书馆的卡片目录里也找不到。

sentences.en: So we started writing our own history.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始书写自己的历史。

sentences.en: And part of writing that history meant drawing attention to Manzanar itself.
sentences.zh: 而书写那段历史的一部分，就意味着吸引人们对曼扎纳本身的关注。

sentences.en: When Warren and Victor found it, the place had no historical designation, no sign, and no plaque.
sentences.zh: 当沃伦和维克托找到它时，这个地方没有任何历史标志、路标或牌匾。

sentences.en: But that was all about to change.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都即将改变。

sentences.en: Warren and Victor drove back to Los Angeles,
sentences.zh: 沃伦和维克托开车回到了洛杉矶，

sentences.en: but they knew they wanted to come back and bring more people with them next time.
sentences.zh: 但他们知道自己想再次回来，下次还要带更多人一起来。

sentences.en: And there's a thing in Japanese called Hakamai-di,
sentences.zh: 日语里有一个词叫“墓参日”（Hakamai-di），

sentences.en: where you have a pilgrimage back to important places.
sentences.zh: 意思是去重要的地方进行朝圣。

sentences.en: And so, on a December morning in 1969,
sentences.zh: 于是，在1969年12月的一个早晨，

sentences.en: over 150 people piled into cars and vans and buses on a pilgrimage to Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 150多人挤进轿车、货车和大巴，踏上了前往曼扎纳的朝圣之旅。

sentences.en: Going to that part of California at that time of year was just stupid.
sentences.zh: 一年中的这个时候去加州的那片地方简直太蠢了。

sentences.en: Cold.
sentences.zh: 冷。

sentences.en: Cold.
sentences.zh: 冷极了。

sentences.en: It was so cold.
sentences.zh: 天气实在太冷了。

sentences.en: But the shivering pilgrims followed Warren and Victor's directions to the cemetery.
sentences.zh: 但瑟瑟发抖的朝圣者们顺着沃伦和维克托指引的方向来到了墓地。

sentences.en: So we cleaned up the cemetery and we brought paint and wire brushes
sentences.zh: 所以我们打扫了墓地，带了油漆和钢丝刷，

sentences.en: and scraped everything down and repainted the monuments.
sentences.zh: 把所有东西都刮干净，并重新粉刷了纪念碑。

sentences.en: We did a lot of work in terms of refurbishing the area.
sentences.zh: 我们在修缮该地区方面做了大量工作。

sentences.en: We knew we were coming back.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们还会回来。

sentences.en: Most of the people on the pilgrimage were younger Japanese Americans
sentences.zh: 朝圣队伍中的大多数人都是从未在集中营待过的年轻日裔美国人。

sentences.en: who had never spent time at camp.
sentences.zh: 但那天也有少数人曾经真正在曼扎纳生活过。

sentences.en: But there were a few people there that day who had actually lived at Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是来自洛杉矶的苏·国富·埃姆里。

sentences.en: One of them was Sue Kunitomi Embry from Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 她最终落入这个荒凉山谷的故事始于1941年。

sentences.en: The story of how she ended up in this desolate valley begins in 1941.
sentences.zh: 我当时18岁。

sentences.en: I was 18.
sentences.zh: 我一月份刚高中毕业，正帮母亲打理一家小杂货店，

sentences.en: I had finished high school in January and I was helping my mother take care of a small grocery store,
sentences.zh: 那是她刚刚在头一年买下的。

sentences.en: which she had purchased just a year before.
sentences.zh: 苏·埃姆里于2006年逝世。

sentences.en: Sue Embry died in 2006.
sentences.zh: 这段音频节选自她2002年接受日裔美国人传承项目Densho采访时的录音。

sentences.en: This audio is from an interview she did with Densho, the Japanese-American legacy project, back in 2002.
sentences.zh: 我们社区收到的通知落款日期是5月3日，我们必须在5月9日离开，

sentences.en: The notice that came to our neighborhood was dated May the 3rd and we had to leave on May the 9th,
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们只有大约五天时间。

sentences.en: which meant we had about five days.
sentences.zh: 只有五天时间收拾好所有行李并向曼扎纳报到。

sentences.en: Five days to pack up all their belongings and report to Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 这个集中营是美国政府为在二战期间关押日裔美国人而建立的10个集中营之一。

sentences.en: The camp was one of 10 set up by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 珍珠港事件发生后，美国的反日种族主义情绪达到狂热顶点。

sentences.en: government to imprison Japanese-Americans during World War II.
sentences.zh: 军方领导人在没有任何证据的情况下，一再质疑所有日本血统居民的忠诚度。

sentences.en: Following the bombing of Pearl Harbor, anti-Japanese racism reached a fever pitch in the United States.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1942年，罗斯福总统签署了第9066号行政令，

sentences.en: Military leaders repeatedly questioned the loyalty of all people of Japanese descent without evidence.
sentences.zh: 为在西海岸关押数千名日裔美国人铺平了道路。

sentences.en: And then, in 1942, President Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066,
sentences.zh: 以下是40年代一部为这一决定辩护的宣传片片段。

sentences.en: paving the way for the incarceration of thousands of Japanese-Americans on the West CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 当日本人袭击珍珠港时，我们的西海岸变成了潜在的战区。

sentences.en: Here's a clip from a 40s propaganda film justifying the decision.
sentences.zh: 生活在该战区内的有10万多名日本血统居民，

sentences.en: When the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbor, our West Coast became a potential combat zone.
sentences.zh: 其中三分之二是美国公民，三分之一是外国侨民。

sentences.en: Living in that zone were more than 100,000 persons of Japanese ancestry,
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们当中有些人具有潜在危险。

sentences.en: two-thirds of them American citizens, one-third aliens.
sentences.zh: 因此，军方当局决定，所有人，不论是公民还是侨民，都必须搬迁。

sentences.en: We knew that some among them were potentially dangerous.
sentences.zh: 大多数家庭不得不仓促出售财产，通常只能卖出原值的九牛一毛。

sentences.en: Military authorities therefore determined that all of them, citizens and aliens alike, would have to move.
sentences.zh: 有些人把房子租出去或者托付给朋友，但另一些人则干脆直接抛弃了房屋。

sentences.en: Most families had to sell property quickly, often at a fraction of its value.
sentences.zh: 5月9日，苏的家人，包括她寡居的母亲以及六个兄弟姐妹，全都来到了火车站。

sentences.en: Some rented out their homes or left them with friends, but others abandoned them altogether.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知只能带上自己拿得动的东西。

sentences.en: On May 9th, Sue's family, her widowed mother and her six brothers and sisters, all went to the train station.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我一直在想，我们是美国公民，他们却这样对我们，我们没有任何权利，没有人为我们发声。

sentences.en: They were told that they could only bring what they could carry with them.
sentences.zh: 他们在黑暗中抵达曼扎纳，找到了分配给他们的营房。

sentences.en: You know, I kept thinking, we're American citizens and they're doing this to us and we have no rights, nobody to speak up for us.
sentences.zh: 集中营被划分为36个住宅区，每个区有14栋营房、两个厕所和一个食堂。

sentences.en: They arrived at Manzanar in the dark and found their way to their assigned barrack.
sentences.zh: 家属通常被允许住在一起。

sentences.en: The camp was divided into 36 residential blocks, each with 14 barracks, two latrines and a mess hall.
sentences.zh: 我们有八张行军床，帆布行军床，没有任何形式的隔断。

sentences.en: Families were usually allowed to sleep together.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都睡在一个大房间里。

sentences.en: We had eight cots, canvas cots, no partitions of any kind.
sentences.zh: 总共有800栋建筑，一万多名居民挤在一平方英里的土地上。

sentences.en: We all slept in one big room.
sentences.zh: 集中营生活中最艰难的部分之一就是完全缺乏隐私。

sentences.en: In total, there were 800 buildings and over 10,000 people packed into one square mile.
sentences.zh: 厕所完全是开放式的、毫无遮挡，淋浴间或马桶之间没有隔间或隔板。

sentences.en: One of the hardest parts of life at camp was the total lack of privacy.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始，像我母亲这样的人会熬夜，希望能趁邻居们都转过身去时去洗个澡。

sentences.en: The latrines were completely open and exposed, with no stalls or dividers between the showers or toilets.
sentences.zh: 但大家都熬夜，也都想在有隐私的情况下洗澡。

sentences.en: So in the beginning, people like my mother would stay up late, hoping to take a shower where her neighbors went around.
sentences.zh: 一道五股铁丝网的围栏环绕着整个集中营，周边设有八座岗楼。

sentences.en: But they all stayed up late and they all wanted to take their shower in privacy.
sentences.zh: 每座岗楼都配有一盏探照灯和一名手持机枪的士兵。

sentences.en: A five-strand barbed wire fence encircled the entire camp, with eight guard towers around the perimeter.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一天晚上我出门，探照灯一路跟着我到了厕所。

sentences.en: Each guard tower had a searchlight and a soldier with a machine gun.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都对那些探照灯记忆犹新。

sentences.en: I remember going out one night and a searchlight followed me all the way to the latrine.
sentences.zh: 曼扎纳无疑是一座监狱，但里面的居民尽其所能把它变成了一个适宜居住的城市。

sentences.en: And I think everyone remembers those searchlights.
sentences.zh: 他们有学校、教堂和俱乐部、棒球场和篮球场。

sentences.en: Manzanar was undoubtedly a prison, but the people inside did everything they could to turn it into a livable city.
sentences.zh: 人们建造岩石花园，种植花卉和蔬菜。

sentences.en: They had schools, churches, and clubs, baseball fields, and basketball courts.
sentences.zh: 这是美化周围环境的真正尝试，我认为这确实提升了人们的士气。

sentences.en: People built rock gardens and planted flowers and vegetables.
sentences.zh: 集中营还有自己的报纸，讽刺地取名为《曼扎纳自由报》，苏·埃姆里曾在该报担任记者和编辑。

sentences.en: It was a real attempt to beautify their surroundings, and I think it really helped the morale of the people.
sentences.zh: 曼扎纳一直运作到战争结束。

sentences.en: The camp also had its own newspaper, ironically called the Manzanar Free Press, where Sue Embry worked as a reporter and editor.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，曾有过几次针对集中营的法律诉讼。

sentences.en: Manzanar operated through the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 但每一次，法庭都维持了关押日裔美国人合宪的判决。

sentences.en: During that time, there were several legal challenges to the camps.
sentences.zh: 1945年11月21日，在美国

sentences.en: But each time, the courts upheld the constitutionality of Japanese-American incarceration.
sentences.zh: 轰炸广岛和长崎几个月后，也就是集中营首次开放近四年后，

sentences.en: On November 21st, 1945, a few months after the U.S.
sentences.zh: 政府永久关闭了曼扎纳，并将其拆毁。

sentences.en: bombed Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and nearly four years after the camp had first opened,
sentences.zh: 各家各户被迫再次搬迁。

sentences.en: the government closed Manzanar for good and dismantled the camp.
sentences.zh: 承担不起自行离开费用的居民会获得一张车票和25美元。

sentences.en: Families were forced to move once again.
sentences.zh: 通常，他们已经没有可以回去的家了。

sentences.en: People who couldn't afford to leave on their own were given a bus ticket and $25.
sentences.zh: 当苏·埃姆里的父母回到洛杉矶时，他们发现自己从前的杂货店和房子已经被拆毁了。

sentences.en: Often, they didn't have a home to go back to.
sentences.zh: 苏·国富·埃姆里离开集中营后，在中西部搬过一阵子家，但最终还是回到了洛杉矶。

sentences.en: When Sue Embry's parents returned to Los Angeles, they found that their old grocery store and house had been demolished.
sentences.zh: 但人们对日裔美国人在战争期间经历的苦难闭口不谈，这让她感到困扰。

sentences.en: After Sue Kunitomi Embry left camp, she moved to the Midwest for a little while, but ultimately ended up back in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 因此，当她听说有一群年轻大学生正前往曼扎纳朝圣时，她决定加入他们。

sentences.en: But it bothered her how little people talked about what Japanese-Americans had been through during the war.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了1969年的那个冬日，当时大约150人前往曼扎纳，以吸引人们关注那里发生过的事情。

sentences.en: So when she heard about a bunch of young college students making a pilgrimage to Manzanar, she decided to join them.
sentences.zh: 12月朝圣时媒体出现了，当时寒风呼啸。

sentences.en: Which brings us back to that winter day in 1969, when around 150 people traveled to Manzanar to draw attention to what had happened there.
sentences.zh: 那是布鲁斯·埃姆里，苏的儿子。

sentences.en: The media showed up at this pilgrimage in December, wind howling very cold.
sentences.zh: 这是什么。

sentences.en: That's Bruce Embry, Sue's son.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个测试。

sentences.en: He says his mom and another person who had also been imprisoned at Manzanar began telling reporters what life had been like there during the war.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的母亲和另一位曾在曼扎纳遭关押的人开始向记者讲述，战争期间那里的生活是怎样的。

sentences.en: And it caused an uproar.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场轩然大波。

sentences.en: I mean, people were just completely aghast that anyone would speak to the broader public outside the confines of the Japanese-American community about what happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家完全震惊了，竟然有人敢向日本裔社群之外的更广泛公众谈论发生的这一切。

sentences.en: The older generation, they were mad.
sentences.zh: 老一辈人，他们很生气。

sentences.en: Again, Warren Furutani, who helped organize the pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 再次有请沃伦·古谷（Warren Furutani），他是朝圣活动的组织者之一。

sentences.en: Why are you bringing this up?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么要提这事？

sentences.en: It's better left forgotten, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最好还是让它随风消逝。

sentences.en: It's, uh, the hatchet's been buried.
sentences.zh: 呃，这已经是过去的事，恩怨已了。

sentences.en: Leave it buried.
sentences.zh: 让它随风消逝吧。

sentences.en: But these activists were just getting started.
sentences.zh: 但这些活动人士才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: Especially Sue Embry.
sentences.zh: 尤其是苏·恩布里（Sue Embry）。

sentences.en: I think the pilgrimage made her understand how important the site was to the community.
sentences.zh: 我认为那次朝圣让她明白了这处遗址对社区有多么重要。

sentences.en: And I think in particular how the community itself had to come to grips with what happened.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，特别是社区本身必须正视所发生的一切。

sentences.en: Following the 1969 pilgrimage, Sue Embry, Warren Furutani, and others formed the Manzanar Committee with the specific goal of getting the site recognized as a historic landmark.
sentences.zh: 在1969年的朝圣活动之后，苏·恩布里、沃伦·古谷等人成立了曼扎纳委员会，其明确目标是争取将该遗址认定为历史地标。

sentences.en: We felt that we needed society to acknowledge this fact, not let it be buried in the back pages or in a simple paragraph in a history book.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们需要社会承认这一事实，而不是让它被埋没在历史书的边角料或简单的一段话里。

sentences.en: They lobbied hard for three years, all the while continuing yearly pilgrimages to the site.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了三年的艰难游说，期间每年都坚持前往该遗址朝圣。

sentences.en: In 1972, the state of California designated Manzanar a state landmark and agreed to install a bronze plaque.
sentences.zh: 1972年，加利福尼亚州将曼扎纳指定为州立历史地标，并同意安装一块青铜牌匾。

sentences.en: It was one of the first public acknowledgments of what had happened there during the war.
sentences.zh: 这是对战争期间那里所发生事情的首次公开承认之一。

sentences.en: So the wording of the plaque became a huge issue.
sentences.zh: 因此，牌匾上的措辞成了一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Particularly the question of what to call Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 尤其是该如何称呼曼扎纳。

sentences.en: Was it a concentration camp?
sentences.zh: 它是集中营吗？

sentences.en: An internment camp?
sentences.zh: 拘留营？

sentences.en: A relocation center?
sentences.zh: 安置中心？

sentences.en: This is still contentious today.
sentences.zh: 这在今天依然充满争议。

sentences.en: Some people don't like the term concentration camp because it's associated with Nazi genocide.
sentences.zh: 有些人不喜欢“集中营”这个词，因为它让人联想到纳粹大屠杀。

sentences.en: Then again, internment camp feels like a euphemism.
sentences.zh: 话又说回来，“拘留营”听起来像是一个委婉的说法。

sentences.en: Don't let my mother-in-law hear someone call it internment camp.
sentences.zh: 别让我岳母听到有人管它叫拘留营。

sentences.en: And she's this 93-year-old, white-haired, petite dynamo.
sentences.zh: 她是一个93岁、满头白发、精力充沛的小个子老人。

sentences.en: She'll kick your ass.
sentences.zh: 她会把你揍得落花流水。

sentences.en: In the end, after a few fiery meetings, the Manzanar committee convinced the state that the plaque should read as follows.
sentences.zh: 最后，经过几次激烈的会议，曼扎纳委员会说服了加州政府，让牌匾上的文字如此写道。

sentences.en: In the early part of World War II, 110,000 persons of Japanese ancestry were interned in relocation centers by Executive Order 9066.
sentences.zh: 在二战初期，根据9066号行政命令，11万名有日本血统的人被关押在安置中心。

sentences.en: Manzanar, the first of 10 such concentration camps, was bounded by barbed wire and guard towers, confining 10,000 persons, the majority of which being American citizens.
sentences.zh: 曼扎纳是此类10个集中营中的第一个，四周环绕着铁丝网和瞭望塔，关押了1万人，其中大多数是美国公民。

sentences.en: May the injustices and humiliation suffered here as a result of hysteria, of racism, and economic exploitation never emerge again.
sentences.zh: 愿因歇斯底里、种族主义和经济剥削而在这里遭受的不公与羞辱，永远不再发生。

sentences.en: 1,500 people attended the 1973 pilgrimage to watch the plaque get installed.
sentences.zh: 1500人参加了1973年的朝圣活动，见证了这块牌匾的安装。

sentences.en: But it didn't go over too well with some folks who lived in nearby towns.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有得到附近城镇一些居民的认可。

sentences.en: Within weeks, they've shot it full of shotgun pellets.
sentences.zh: 几周之内，他们就用猎枪弹把牌匾打得千疮百孔。

sentences.en: Someone took an axe to it to try and chisel off the word racism.
sentences.zh: 有人甚至用斧子去凿掉“种族主义”这个词。

sentences.en: You can still see the bullet holes on the plaque today.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，你依然能在牌匾上看到弹孔。

sentences.en: But Sue Embry and the Manzanar committee were undeterred.
sentences.zh: 但苏·恩布里和曼扎纳委员会并没有被吓退。

sentences.en: In fact, they were already thinking bigger.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们的目标已经放得更远。

sentences.en: They wanted Manzanar to be a national historic site.
sentences.zh: 他们希望曼扎纳成为国家历史遗址。

sentences.en: It's important to note that all this was occurring alongside a larger fight for redress and reparations.
sentences.zh: 需要指出的是，这一切都是与争取平反和赔偿的更大斗争同时进行的。

sentences.en: Several Japanese-American organizations had demanded an official apology from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 几个日裔美国人组织曾要求美国政府进行正式道歉，

sentences.en: government and payments for those who had been incarcerated during the war.
sentences.zh: 并向在战争期间被关押的人支付赔偿金。

sentences.en: And in 1988, President Reagan signed the Civil Liberties Act, giving $20,000 in reparations to every living person who had been sent to a camp.
sentences.zh: 1988年，里根总统签署了《公民自由法案》，向每一位在世的曾被送往集中营的人支付2万美元赔偿金。

sentences.en: Yet no payment can make up for those lost years.
sentences.zh: 然而，任何赔偿都无法弥补那些失去的岁月。

sentences.en: So what is most important in this bill has less to do with property than with honor.
sentences.zh: 因此，这项法案最重要的地方与其说关乎财产，不如说关乎荣誉。

sentences.en: For here, we admit a wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为在这里，我们承认了错误。

sentences.en: Here, we reaffirm our commitment as a nation to equal justice under the law.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们重申了作为一个国家对法律面前人人平等的承诺。

sentences.en: Sue Embry was very involved in the redress movement.
sentences.zh: 苏·恩布里极力参与了这场平反运动。

sentences.en: And she wanted to keep the momentum going in the fight to get Manzanar turned into a national historic site.
sentences.zh: 她希望保持这股势头，继续争取将曼扎纳转为国家历史遗址。

sentences.en: But the Manzanar committee faced stiff opposition from the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.
sentences.zh: 但曼扎纳委员会遭到了洛杉矶水电局的强烈反对。

sentences.en: The DWP actually owned the land and the rights to its water.
sentences.zh: 水电局实际上拥有这片土地及其水权。

sentences.en: So here comes this middle-aged woman saying, no, this land is really significant to us, our community, and to the region itself.
sentences.zh: 于是，这个中年妇女站出来说，不，这片土地对我们、对我们的社区以及整个地区都有着重大的意义。

sentences.en: And we want it to be a national park.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它成为一个国家公园。

sentences.en: Well, the DWP didn't want to have any part of that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，水电局对此根本不感兴趣。

sentences.en: The Manzanar committee ended up drafting legislation for Congress.
sentences.zh: 曼扎纳委员会最终起草了提交给国会的法案。

sentences.en: And Sue Embry flew to Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 苏·恩布里飞往华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: to testify before the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美军参议院公共土地、国家公园和森林小组委员会前作证。

sentences.en: Senate Subcommittee on Public Lands, National Parks, and Forests.
sentences.zh: 她说，民主是一个脆弱的概念，它取决于践行它的人民有多优秀、多坚强。

sentences.en: She says, democracy is a fragile concept, only as good and strong as the people who practice it.
sentences.zh: 让我们向世界宣告，我们是一个坚强而坚定的人民，我们承认过去的错误，以便在未来不再重蹈覆辙。

sentences.en: Let us tell the world that we are a people, strong and resolute, acknowledging the errors of our past in order not to repeat them in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，这就是曼扎纳历史遗址能够留给子孙后代的遗产。

sentences.en: And this is the legacy which we believe the Manzanar Historic Site can leave for future generations.
sentences.zh: 该法案获得通过，1992年3月3日，曼扎纳被宣布为国家历史遗址。

sentences.en: The legislation passed, and on March 3rd, 1992, Manzanar was declared a National Historic Site.
sentences.zh: 但除了公墓之外，那里几乎什么都没有。

sentences.en: But apart from the cemetery, there was hardly anything there.
sentences.zh: 国家公园管理局必须决定他们想如何纪念这段不公正的历史。

sentences.en: The National Park Service had to decide how they wanted to memorialize this injustice.
sentences.zh: 他们成立了一个委员会，其中包含曾在曼扎纳被关押过的人，

sentences.en: They formed a committee that included people who had been incarcerated at Manzanar,
sentences.zh: 委员会决定，他们不希望只是建一个博物馆，让游客在标牌上阅读发生了什么。

sentences.en: and the committee decided that they didn't just want a museum where visitors could read about what happened on placards.
sentences.zh: 他们希望按照战争期间的原貌重建部分集中营，

sentences.en: They wanted to rebuild portions of the camp exactly as they had been during the war,
sentences.zh: 这样游客就能亲身感受到那里的生活是怎样的。

sentences.en: so that visitors could feel what life had been like.
sentences.zh: 所以你走进去，这是一个空房间，尽管我们有一张行军床、一叠陆军毛毯和一叠床垫套，

sentences.en: So you walk in, it's an empty room, although we have a cot and a stack of army blankets and a stack of mattress covers,
sentences.zh: 还有一堆靠墙摆放的行军床。

sentences.en: and a bunch of cots up against the wall.
sentences.zh: 这是曼扎纳国家历史遗址的埃莉萨·林奇（Elisa Lynch），她正带我参观一栋重建的营房。

sentences.en: This is Elisa Lynch of the Manzanar National Historic Site, showing me a rebuilt barrack.
sentences.zh: 她说，他们努力想要还原真实面貌，但它仍然没有1942年人们刚到这里时那么严酷。

sentences.en: She says they tried hard to get it right, but it's still not as harsh as it would have been when people arrived here back in 1942.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时本该有尘土从地板缝隙里吹进来。

sentences.en: I mean, there should be dirt blowing up through the floor.
sentences.zh: 建筑物应该嘎吱作响。

sentences.en: The building should be creaking.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们有两种选择：要么按原样重建，

sentences.en: The thing is, we had the option of either building them as they were,
sentences.zh: 但不允许人们走进去，因为它们对访客来说不够安全。

sentences.en: but not allowing people to walk in, because they wouldn't be safe for people to come into.
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以按照抗震标准和无障碍标准重建，而这正是我们选择的做法。

sentences.en: Or we could rebuild them to earthquake standards, accessibility standards, and that's what we chose to do.
sentences.zh: 外面是一个铺着白色铁环的泥地篮球场，

sentences.en: Outside, there's a dirt basketball court with white metal hoops,
sentences.zh: 还有一条单行道，在曾经的营地里蜿蜒曲折地延伸。

sentences.en: and a one-way road tracing a long and winding circuit through what used to be the camp.
sentences.zh: 沿途的路标显示着曾经特定建筑所在的位置。

sentences.en: Signposts along the way show where specific buildings once stood.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，破碎的混凝土基底和岩石花园的遗迹仍然清晰可见，或是已被发掘出土。

sentences.en: In some places, cracked concrete foundations and the remains of rock gardens are still visible or have been unearthed.
sentences.zh: 在远处，你可以看到一座重建的瞭望塔。

sentences.en: In the distance, you can see a rebuilt guard tower.
sentences.zh: 它有40英尺高，木质格子墙壁，顶部装有一个巨大的探照灯。

sentences.en: It's 40 feet tall, with latticed wood sides and a giant searchlight at the top.
sentences.zh: 这非常有争议，因为许多当地人尤其不希望这里有一座瞭望塔，

sentences.en: It was very controversial, because a lot of the locals especially did not want it to have a guard tower,
sentences.zh: 因为人们不希望它给社区带来不好的影响。

sentences.en: because people don't want it to reflect badly on the community.
sentences.zh: 但公园管理局继续向那些真正曾在营地生活过的人寻求指导。

sentences.en: But the Park Service continued to seek guidance from folks who had actually lived at the camp.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，人们一次又一次地说，

sentences.en: Over time, people have said over and over,
sentences.zh: 最需要展示的东西是瞭望塔和厕所。

sentences.en: the most important thing to show are the guard towers and the latrines.
sentences.zh: 我甚至听人真切地说过，你知道，很高兴你们建了游客中心。

sentences.en: I've had people literally say, you know, we're glad you have the visitor center.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很喜欢你们保留了营房。

sentences.en: We really like that you have the barracks.
sentences.zh: 但如果不亲自走进去看看那一排厕所，没有人会真正理解。

sentences.en: But no one will ever understand until they go in and see that row of toilets.
sentences.zh: 埃莉萨·林奇带我来到了遗址最新增设的景点——一个女性厕所的复制品。

sentences.en: Elisa Lynch takes me to the site's newest addition, a replica of a woman's latrine.
sentences.zh: 我参观时这座建筑尚未对公众开放，但她带我进去参观了内部。

sentences.en: The building wasn't open to the public when I visited, but she showed me inside.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个开放式的房间。

sentences.en: It's just an open room.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个长水槽和一排五个马桶，彼此之间没有隔板。

sentences.en: There's a long trough sink and a row of five toilets with no dividers between them.
sentences.zh: 你总是一次又一次地听到关于羞辱的诉说。

sentences.en: You hear over and over about the humiliation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我听女性谈起在公共场合经历初潮，

sentences.en: You know, I've heard women talk about having your first period in public,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这对所有人、所有女性来说都是非常私人的事情。

sentences.en: you know, which I think is a very personal thing to all people, all women.
sentences.zh: 而这里毫无隐私可言。

sentences.en: And there's no privacy here.
sentences.zh: 林奇与数百名曾在曼扎纳生活过的人交谈过。

sentences.en: Lynch has spoken with hundreds of people who lived at Manzanar.
sentences.zh: 他们对那段在营地生活的时光有着不同的看法。

sentences.en: And they all have different perspectives on their time at camp.
sentences.zh: 有些人深情地回忆起他们在这里建立的友谊。

sentences.en: Some people fondly remember the friendships they built here.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则说这段经历撕裂了他们的家庭。

sentences.en: Others say the experience tore their family apart.
sentences.zh: 没错，这里有棒球队。

sentences.en: Yes, it had baseball teaMs.
sentences.zh: 但这里也有120名武装士兵。

sentences.en: It also had 120 armed soldiers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是的，这里有美丽的庭院，但这里也有瞭望塔。

sentences.en: You know, yes, it had beautiful gardens, but it also had guard towers.
sentences.zh: 她只是希望这个遗址能够展现这里所发生的事情那段完整而纷繁复杂的历史。

sentences.en: She just wants the site to show the full, messy history of what happened here.
sentences.zh: 我认为国家公园代表了美国最好的一面，也代表了美国人最好的一面。

sentences.en: I think the national parks represent America at its best, and Americans at their beSt.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，审视我们做得不够好的那些时光同样很有意义。

sentences.en: And I think it's also good that we look at the times when we haven't been our beSt.
sentences.zh: 这对未来是一堂生动的课。

sentences.en: And it's a lesson for the future.
sentences.zh: 这个遗址之所以存在，这个国家公园之所以存在，是因为普通人们付出了努力，确保他们的故事没有被风吹散，

sentences.en: This site exists, this national park exists because of the efforts of ordinary people to make sure that their story wasn't swept away by the wind
sentences.zh: 也没有被那些不愿想起我们过去某些人软弱面的人所掩埋。

sentences.en: or buried by those that don't want to be reminded of the weaknesses of some in our paSt.
sentences.zh: 又见布鲁斯·恩布里（Bruce Embry）。

sentences.en: That's Bruce Embry again.
sentences.zh: 每年春天，他都是成百上千名来到曼扎纳参加年度朝圣活动的人之一。

sentences.en: Every spring, he's one of the hundreds, if not thousands, of people who come to Manzanar for the annual pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 就是那个始于1969年的活动。

sentences.en: The one that started back in 1969.
sentences.zh: 他们举行宗教仪式和击鼓表演，共同缅怀这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: They hold religious ceremonies and drumming performances and remember what happened here together.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是为了日裔美国人。

sentences.en: But it's not just for Japanese Americans.
sentences.zh: 最近，自9·11事件以来，朝圣活动几乎总是会邀请一位来自穆斯林社群的发言人。

sentences.en: Lately, since 9-11, the pilgrimage has almost always had a speaker from the Muslim community.
sentences.zh: 近年来，领导朝圣活动的活动人士一直试图将战时对日裔美国人的歧视，

sentences.en: In recent years, the activists who lead the pilgrimage have tried to connect the wartime discrimination against Japanese Americans
sentences.zh: 与当代以安全为名对美籍穆斯林的歧视联系起来。

sentences.en: with contemporary discrimination against Muslim Americans in the name of security.
sentences.zh: 指出与当今事件的相似之处真的非常重要。

sentences.en: It's really important that the parallels to what's happening today get raised.
